### [Gemini Decisions API](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/11/gemini-decisions-api/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-11-11

Google has launched Gemini Decision 1, a multimodal decision model API competing with Jev and OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna.

- Gemini Decision 1 supports yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring question types, adopting Jev's 'Noul' terminology for yes/no queries.
- It is priced at $0.10 per million input tokens with free output, matching GPT-6 Luna, whereas Jev costs $0.042 per million input tokens.
- The model accepts multimodal inputs including text, images, audio, video, and PDFs, unlike text-only Jev or text/image OpenAI models.
- Unlike Jev and OpenAI which output binary 1.0 or 0.0 values for yes/no questions, Gemini Decision 1 returns continuous probability scores.

**Why it matters:** It provides a cost-effective, fully multimodal API for structured decision-making tasks across video, audio, and documents with fine-grained probability outputs.

`gemini` `ai` `api` `llm-release` `multimodal`

### [Anthropic's IPO roadshow video](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/11/anthropic-ipo-roadshow/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-11-11

Anthropic's IPO roadshow revealed details on their multi-chip infrastructure and the use of an internal model to autonomously port Claude to AMD GPUs in three days.

- Anthropic trains and serves Claude across four chip families: AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs.
- Using an internal model named Mythos, Anthropic ported Claude to AMD GPUs in three days with virtually no human intervention, with Claude writing or porting nearly 100% of the kernels.
- Anthropic measures compute using 'total effective compute', calculated as physical capacity multiplied by stacked, compound compute multipliers.
- The company aims to leverage recursive self-improvement by using Claude to autonomously discover new compute multipliers.

**Why it matters:** Autonomous model-driven kernel porting drastically lowers the engineering overhead required to utilize diverse hardware architectures, reducing single-vendor compute lock-in.

`anthropic` `gpus` `claude` `infrastructure` `hardware`
